title: Bob and Ray
paragraphs: Bob Elliott and Ray Goulding's long-running satirical comedy, built from deadpan sketches that spoofed broadcasting, advertising, interviews, soap operas, and everyday American life.

Bob Elliott and Ray Goulding’s long-running deadpan comedy/satire partnership. The historical broadcasts combined ad-libbed talk, sketches, mock interviews, serial parodies, characters, music and fake/real commercials across local, network and public radio.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: WHDH Boston era (1946 to July 1, 1951) on [[org|org.957c02c01469be51|WHDH]], NBC network era (July 2, 1951 to October 9, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], NBC Monitor participation (1955 to 1959) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Mutual daily era (October 3, 1955 to September 20, 1957) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].
The stories often return to Soap opera parody, Mock interviews, Advertising parody, Journalism, Book reviewing, and Sports broadcasting.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar radio culture as material for satire, Bob and Ray across the network-radio/television transition, and Advertising culture and Bob and Ray’s mock commercials.
